key_insight: The paper reports that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can learn to use real robots through reinforcement learning conducted entirely in simulation, without demonstrations.
problem_solved: Open-weight robot-use agents have lagged behind frontier proprietary models. This work addresses how to train a more capable open-weight agent without demonstrations or real-world training.
method: Start with an open-weight reasoning model containing 27 billion parameters.
Train robot-use capabilities through reinforcement learning entirely in simulation, without demonstrations.
Apply the resulting agent to real robots; the provided abstract excerpt does not specify the transfer procedure or evaluation results.
impact: The reported result suggests a path toward capable robot-use agents built on open-weight models while avoiding real-world training requirements. Quantitative performance and generalization cannot be assessed from the truncated abstract.
visual_elements: Pipeline: 27B reasoning model → reinforcement learning in simulation → real robot.
Side-by-side illustration of a simulated robot and its physical counterpart.
Conceptual comparison of proprietary and open-weight robot-use agents, without unsupported performance values.
paper_title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
paper_authors: Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo, Fangzhou Zhao, Yilong Zhao
